acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Treants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Oakheart, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Vine-Lane Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Broad oak-form, heavy root legs, dense foliage, hanging vines, and a clear bark face; still no hollow cavity.
Signature mechanic: Root Loom: two arm vines knot to one heavy root, drawing foliage walls together while the unknotted lane remains open.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a controller that braids hanging vines between heavy roots to define one moving safe lane.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T3 have no heartwood cavity, no waterfall, no boulders, and no groves; T4 alone gains the source-supported heartwood cavity; T5 alone carries its waterfall, boulders, and groves.
Char-controlled bark plates, resin fuel channels, ember-pruned branch tips, directional smoke vents, and blackened firebreak seams add combustion while preserving living growth.
counterplay: Take the unknotted lane and cut the visible braid at the selected root to drop both foliage walls. Affinity signal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T3 have no heartwood cavity, no waterfall, no boulders, and no groves, so a resin channel exposes a root seam; T4 heartwood cavity opens after venting; T5 waterfall, boulders, and groves reveal one firebreak root when the canopy burns.
identityInvariants: Vertical trunk body, root-cluster legs, long branch arms, a bark-suggested face, and canopy remain recognizable.
Bark brown and grey, moss green, autumn gold, sap, and restrained amber heartwood remain botanical materials.
Nests, vines, mushrooms, bark runes, scars, and growth rings record age without replacing readable joints.
Girth, canopy, rooted reach, and resident ecosystems escalate while branch load and root commitment preserve counterplay.
telegraph: The clear bark face looks toward one root as two hanging vines twist around it.
